31	general rules engine: plan-gated (the flag is on once the org's plan reaches a threshold,
32	per `PLAN_ORDER`), percentage rollout (deterministic per organization, not per user, so a
33	whole organization sees consistent behavior rather than individual members randomly
34	diverging), boolean-always-on (`command_palette`), and role-gated (the flag is on once the
35	acting user's role reaches a threshold, used by `issue_templates`). Every flag in the
36	registry declares exactly one of these strategies plus whether it is `overridable`.
37	
38	Ten flags exist today: `kanban_board` (plan >= starter, overridable), `ai_issue_summary`
39	(percentage 25, overridable), `command_palette` (always on, not overridable),
40	`activity_feed` (plan >= growth, overridable), `public_projects` (plan >= enterprise,
41	overridable), `webhooks` (plan >= growth, not overridable), `csv_export` (plan >= starter,
42	overridable), `digest_email` (plan >= growth, overridable), `issue_templates` (role >=
43	admin, overridable), and `advanced_search` (plan >= enterprise, overridable). `webhooks` and
44	`command_palette` are the only two flags marked not overridable — for `command_palette`
45	because there is no reason to ever turn off a zero-cost client affordance, and for
46	`webhooks` because the plan-tier gate on webhooks is a monetization boundary the product
47	team does not want individual support interactions to erode by ad hoc override.
48	
49	Organization-level overrides live in `Organization.settings` (`REQ-005`, defined in
50	`organizations.md`), which is why this document does not restate the storage location but
51	does define the override's evaluation semantics: an override only takes effect for flags
52	whose definition marks them `overridable`, and `toggleFlag` — the only mutator — requires
53	`org:manage_flags`, whose `ROLE_MATRIX` minimum is `admin`.
54	
55	`src/config/nav.ts`'s `visibleNav` is a second, independent consumer of the flag system worth
56	naming here even though it belongs conceptually to navigation rather than to flags: each
57	`NavItem` optionally names both a `PermissionAction` and a `FeatureFlagKey`, and `visibleNav`
58	filters the sidebar and settings navigation trees by calling both `can()` and `isEnabled()`
59	for every item, so a flagged-off feature's settings link disappears from navigation the same
60	tick the flag itself would refuse the underlying action — there is no separate "hide the
61	nav item" maintenance step distinct from the flag definition driving the behavior it gates.
62	
63	## Open questions
64	
65	1. `REQ-189`'s percentage rollout is deterministic per organization, but this document does
66	   not specify the hashing input beyond "per organization" — whether it is stable across a
67	   flag's own lifetime (so an org does not flip in and out of a 25% rollout as unrelated
68	   registry changes are deployed) is an implementation property not independently pinned
69	   down by a requirement.
70	2. `REQ-187`'s four strategies do not include a strategy that combines two conditions (for
71	   example, plan-gated AND percentage), so a flag needing both would require either two
72	   flags or an ad hoc extension — not currently a real need, but a known limitation of the
73	   registry's shape.
74	3. Whether `toggleFlag`'s audit trail (`REQ-192`) distinguishes an override being set to
75	   `true` versus explicitly set to `false` (forcing a normally-on-by-plan flag off) from an
76	   override simply being cleared is not addressed here.
77	4. The role-gated strategy (`issue_templates`, `admin` minimum) evaluates against the
78	   acting user's role at request time, which raises a question none of the eleven
79	   requirements below directly answers: whether a snapshot taken for a page render should be
80	   invalidated the instant that user's role changes mid-session, or whether it is acceptable
81	   for a stale snapshot to grant access for the remainder of an already-rendered page.
82	
83	### REQ-185 — Flags are declared in a single registry
84	
85	- **Priority:** must
86	- **Status:** implemented
87	- **Related:** ADR-012, REQ-195, DES-200
88	- **Implemented by:** `src/config/feature-flags.ts` — `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS`
89	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`
90	
91	`FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS` in `src/config/feature-flags.ts` is the only place a flag's key,
92	strategy, and overridability are declared. No service defines its own ad hoc flag check;
93	every gated behavior in the product traces back to one entry in this table.
94	
95	**Acceptance criteria**
96	
97	1. Every `FeatureFlagKey` used anywhere in the codebase has a corresponding entry in
98	   `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS`.
99	2. Adding a new gated feature requires exactly one new registry entry, not scattered
100	   conditionals.
101	3. The registry is a plain data structure, not a function, so its contents can be
102	   enumerated and documented without executing code.
103	
104	### REQ-186 — Flag evaluation goes through one function
105	
106	- **Priority:** must
107	- **Status:** implemented
108	- **Related:** REQ-185, DES-200
109	
110	`isEnabled(key, context)` in `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` is the sole evaluator, called from
111	both server code (services, jobs) and client components (through the snapshot, `REQ-194`).
112	No caller re-implements a strategy's logic locally; everything defers to this one function.
113	
114	**Acceptance criteria**
115	
116	1. Every call site checking a flag calls `isEnabled`, not a hand-rolled plan or role
117	   comparison that happens to match a flag's intent.
118	2. `isEnabled` is pure given its inputs — the same `(key, context)` pair always yields the
119	   same result for a given registry state.
120	3. `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts` exercises all four strategies through this one
121	   function.
122	
123	**Implemented by:** `src/lib/feature-flags.ts`
124	**Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`
125	
126	### REQ-187 — Four evaluation strategies are supported
127	
128	- **Priority:** must
129	- **Status:** implemented
130	- **Related:** ADR-012, REQ-188, REQ-189
131	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` — `isEnabled`, `src/config/feature-flags.ts`
132	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`
133	
134	Plan-gated, percentage rollout, always-on, and role-gated are the complete set. Every entry
135	in `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS` declares exactly one; there is no flag with a hybrid or custom
136	strategy, which is the constraint `ADR-012` accepted in exchange for a registry simple enough
137	to audit at a glance.
138	
139	**Acceptance criteria**
140	
141	1. `isEnabled`'s implementation has exactly one branch per strategy kind, exhaustively
142	   covering the strategy union type.
143	2. A flag definition missing a strategy field fails validation at load time rather than
144	   defaulting to some implicit behavior.
145	3. Each of the ten current flags maps to exactly one of the four strategies as documented in
146	   the Context section above.
147	
148	### REQ-188 — Plan-gated flags follow the plan ladder
149	
150	- **Priority:** must
151	- **Status:** implemented
152	- **Related:** REQ-131, REQ-050, REQ-120
153	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` — `isEnabled`, `src/config/plan-limits.ts` — `planAtLeast`
154	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`
155	
156	A plan-gated flag's threshold is one of the four plan values, and evaluation uses
157	`planAtLeast(org.plan, threshold)` — the same ordering `PLAN_ORDER` establishes for
158	`REQ-131`'s downgrade logic — so a plan-gated flag is automatically consistent with billing's
159	own notion of "higher plan," rather than maintaining an independent comparison.
160	
161	**Acceptance criteria**
162	
163	1. `kanban_board`, `activity_feed`, `public_projects`, `csv_export`, `digest_email` and
164	   `advanced_search` all evaluate via `planAtLeast`.
165	2. An org's plan-gated flag state changes automatically and immediately when
166	   `billing.plan_changed` takes effect, without a separate flag-specific update step.
167	3. `webhooks` is plan-gated at `growth` exactly like `activity_feed` and `digest_email`, but
168	   is additionally marked non-overridable, distinguishing the gating threshold from the
169	   override policy.
170	
171	### REQ-189 — Percentage rollout is deterministic per organization
172	
173	- **Priority:** should
174	- **Status:** implemented
175	- **Related:** REQ-187, DES-210
176	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` — `isEnabled`
177	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`
178	
179	`ai_issue_summary`'s percentage-25 strategy hashes the organization's id (not the acting
180	user's) to decide whether that org falls inside the rollout percentage, so every member of a
181	given organization sees the same on/off state for the flag — there is no scenario where two
182	members of the same org disagree about whether `ai_issue_summary` is available to them
183	because of random per-request evaluation.
184	
185	**Acceptance criteria**
186	
187	1. Repeated evaluations of `isEnabled('ai_issue_summary', context)` for the same
188	   organization return the same result across calls, absent a registry change.
189	2. Two organizations, given a large enough sample, land in the rollout at approximately the
190	   registry's configured percentage.
191	3. The rollout decision does not depend on the acting user, only the organization.
192	
193	### REQ-190 — Some flags are not overridable
194	
195	- **Priority:** must
196	- **Status:** implemented
197	- **Related:** REQ-152, REQ-191, DES-220
198	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` — `isEnabled`, `src/server/services/feature-flag-service.ts` — `toggleFlag`, `buildFlagContext`
199	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`
200	
201	`command_palette` and `webhooks` are marked `overridable: false` in their registry entries;
202	`toggleFlag` and `buildFlagContext`'s override lookup both must respect this — an override
203	value stored in `Organization.settings` for a non-overridable flag, however it might get
204	there, has no effect on evaluation.
205	
206	**Acceptance criteria**
207	
208	1. `isEnabled` for a non-overridable flag ignores any stored override and evaluates purely
209	   by strategy.
210	2. `toggleFlag` on a non-overridable flag key is rejected before it writes anything to
211	   `Organization.settings`.
212	3. The distinction between "overridable but currently off" and "not overridable" is visible
213	   in the flags settings UI, so an admin is not left wondering why a toggle has no effect.
214	
215	### REQ-191 — Per-organization overrides live in organization settings
216	
217	- **Priority:** must
218	- **Status:** implemented
219	- **Related:** REQ-005, REQ-192
220	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` — `isEnabled`, `src/server/services/feature-flag-service.ts` — `buildFlagContext`
221	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`
222	
223	This document is the evaluation-side complement to `REQ-005` in `organizations.md`, which
224	describes the storage location. Here, the requirement is about precedence: when an override
225	exists for an overridable flag, `isEnabled` uses the override's value directly rather than
226	falling through to the strategy evaluation, regardless of what the strategy would have
227	computed.
228	
229	**Acceptance criteria**
230	
231	1. An override of `true` on a flag whose plan-gated strategy would otherwise evaluate
232	   `false` results in the flag being enabled for that org.
233	2. An override of `false` on a flag whose strategy would otherwise evaluate `true` results
234	   in the flag being disabled for that org.
235	3. Clearing the override reverts evaluation to the underlying strategy, with no residual
236	   effect from the cleared value.
237	
238	### REQ-192 — Toggling a flag requires admin and emits flag.toggled
239	
240	- **Priority:** must
241	- **Status:** implemented
242	- **Related:** REQ-024, DES-071
243	- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/feature-flag-service.ts` — `toggleFlag`
244	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`
245	
246	`toggleFlag(actor, input)` requires `org:manage_flags` (`admin` minimum) and, on success,
247	emits `flag.toggled` with the flag key and new override value, which the activity service
248	records — an important audit trail entry, since a flag override can enable or disable
249	product surface area for an entire organization in one action.
250	
251	**Acceptance criteria**
252	
253	1. A `member` calling `toggleFeatureFlagAction` is denied regardless of which flag they
254	   target.
255	2. `flag.toggled`'s payload identifies the flag key and the resulting override state
256	   (enabled, disabled, or cleared).
257	3. `toggleFlag` on a non-overridable flag fails before emitting the event (`REQ-190`), since
258	   no actual change occurred.
259	
260	### REQ-193 — A disabled feature fails with FeatureDisabledError
261	
262	- **Priority:** must
263	- **Status:** implemented
264	- **Related:** ADR-014, REQ-138
265	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/errors.ts` — `toAppError`
266	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/errors.test.ts`
267	
268	Attempting a gated action while its flag is off throws `FeatureDisabledError`, mapped by
269	`toAppError` to a distinct, specific `AppErrorShape` — not folded into `forbidden` or
270	`validation_failed` — so a client can distinguish "you don't have permission" from "this
271	isn't available on your plan or hasn't been rolled out to you yet" and render the
272	appropriate upsell or explanation.
273	
274	**Acceptance criteria**
275	
276	1. Every gated Server Action checks `isEnabled` and throws `FeatureDisabledError` rather
277	   than silently no-opping when the flag is off.
278	2. `FeatureDisabledError`'s mapped error code is distinct from `forbidden` and
279	   `plan_limit_exceeded`.
280	3. `tests/lib/errors.test.ts` covers `FeatureDisabledError`'s mapping alongside every other
281	   domain error class.
282	
283	### REQ-194 — The client receives a flag snapshot, not the registry
284	
285	- **Priority:** must
286	- **Status:** implemented
287	- **Related:** REQ-186, DES-230
288	- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` — `snapshotFlags`
289	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`
290	
291	`snapshotFlags()` produces a `FeatureFlagSnapshot` — a plain map of flag key to resolved
292	boolean for the current actor and org — that server components pass down to client
293	components, rather than shipping `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS` itself to the browser. This
294	keeps rollout percentages and plan thresholds server-side implementation detail, not
295	something inspectable from client-side JavaScript.
296	
297	**Acceptance criteria**
298	
299	1. No client bundle includes `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS` or the percentage-rollout hash
300	   input.
301	2. `FeatureFlagSnapshot` is computed once per request server-side and passed down, not
302	   recomputed independently by client components calling `isEnabled` themselves with a
303	   client-only context.
304	3. The snapshot reflects the same overrides and strategy evaluation the server would apply
305	   to a Server Action call in the same request.
306	
307	### REQ-195 — Flag keys are a closed union
308	
309	- **Priority:** must
310	- **Status:** implemented
311	- **Related:** REQ-185, DES-200
312	- **Implemented by:** `src/types/feature-flag.ts`, `src/schemas/feature-flag.ts`
313	- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`
314	
315	`FeatureFlagKey` in `src/types/feature-flag.ts` is a closed string-literal union matching
316	exactly the ten keys in `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS`; `src/schemas/feature-flag.ts` validates
317	any client-supplied flag key (for `toggleFeatureFlagAction`'s input) against this same union
318	at runtime, so a request naming an unknown flag key fails validation before it ever reaches
319	`toggleFlag`.
320	
321	**Acceptance criteria**
322	
323	1. `FeatureFlagKey`'s type and `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS`'s keys are kept in lockstep; a
324	   registry entry without a corresponding type member is a type error.
325	2. `toggleFeatureFlagSchema` rejects any flag key not in the closed union at the schema
326	   layer, before authorization or business logic runs.
327	3. Adding an eleventh flag requires updating both the type and the registry in the same
328	   change, never one without the other.

- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** ADR-012, REQ-188, REQ-189
- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` — `isEnabled`, `src/config/feature-flags.ts`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`

Plan-gated, percentage rollout, always-on, and role-gated are the complete set. Every entry
in `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS` declares exactly one; there is no flag with a hybrid or custom
strategy, which is the constraint `ADR-012` accepted in exchange for a registry simple enough
to audit at a glance.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `isEnabled`'s implementation has exactly one branch per strategy kind, exhaustively
   covering the strategy union type.
2. A flag definition missing a strategy field fails validation at load time rather than
   defaulting to some implicit behavior.
3. Each of the ten current flags maps to exactly one of the four strategies as documented in
   the Context section above.

### REQ-188 — Plan-gated flags follow the plan ladder

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-131, REQ-050, REQ-120
- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` — `isEnabled`, `src/config/plan-limits.ts` — `planAtLeast`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`

A plan-gated flag's threshold is one of the four plan values, and evaluation uses
`planAtLeast(org.plan, threshold)` — the same ordering `PLAN_ORDER` establishes for
`REQ-131`'s downgrade logic — so a plan-gated flag is automatically consistent with billing's
own notion of "higher plan," rather than maintaining an independent comparison.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `kanban_board`, `activity_feed`, `public_projects`, `csv_export`, `digest_email` and
   `advanced_search` all evaluate via `planAtLeast`.
2. An org's plan-gated flag state changes automatically and immediately when
   `billing.plan_changed` takes effect, without a separate flag-specific update step.
3. `webhooks` is plan-gated at `growth` exactly like `activity_feed` and `digest_email`, but
   is additionally marked non-overridable, distinguishing the gating threshold from the
   override policy.

### REQ-189 — Percentage rollout is deterministic per organization

- **Priority:** should
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-187, DES-210
- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` — `isEnabled`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`

`ai_issue_summary`'s percentage-25 strategy hashes the organization's id (not the acting
user's) to decide whether that org falls inside the rollout percentage, so every member of a
given organization sees the same on/off state for the flag — there is no scenario where two
members of the same org disagree about whether `ai_issue_summary` is available to them
because of random per-request evaluation.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. Repeated evaluations of `isEnabled('ai_issue_summary', context)` for the same
   organization return the same result across calls, absent a registry change.
2. Two organizations, given a large enough sample, land in the rollout at approximately the
   registry's configured percentage.
3. The rollout decision does not depend on the acting user, only the organization.

### REQ-190 — Some flags are not overridable

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-152, REQ-191, DES-220
- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` — `isEnabled`, `src/server/services/feature-flag-service.ts` — `toggleFlag`, `buildFlagContext`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`

`command_palette` and `webhooks` are marked `overridable: false` in their registry entries;
`toggleFlag` and `buildFlagContext`'s override lookup both must respect this — an override
value stored in `Organization.settings` for a non-overridable flag, however it might get
there, has no effect on evaluation.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `isEnabled` for a non-overridable flag ignores any stored override and evaluates purely
   by strategy.
2. `toggleFlag` on a non-overridable flag key is rejected before it writes anything to
   `Organization.settings`.
3. The distinction between "overridable but currently off" and "not overridable" is visible
   in the flags settings UI, so an admin is not left wondering why a toggle has no effect.

### REQ-191 — Per-organization overrides live in organization settings

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-005, REQ-192
- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` — `isEnabled`, `src/server/services/feature-flag-service.ts` — `buildFlagContext`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`

This document is the evaluation-side complement to `REQ-005` in `organizations.md`, which
describes the storage location. Here, the requirement is about precedence: when an override
exists for an overridable flag, `isEnabled` uses the override's value directly rather than
falling through to the strategy evaluation, regardless of what the strategy would have
computed.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. An override of `true` on a flag whose plan-gated strategy would otherwise evaluate
   `false` results in the flag being enabled for that org.
2. An override of `false` on a flag whose strategy would otherwise evaluate `true` results
   in the flag being disabled for that org.
3. Clearing the override reverts evaluation to the underlying strategy, with no residual
   effect from the cleared value.

### REQ-192 — Toggling a flag requires admin and emits flag.toggled

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-024, DES-071
- **Implemented by:** `src/server/services/feature-flag-service.ts` — `toggleFlag`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`

`toggleFlag(actor, input)` requires `org:manage_flags` (`admin` minimum) and, on success,
emits `flag.toggled` with the flag key and new override value, which the activity service
records — an important audit trail entry, since a flag override can enable or disable
product surface area for an entire organization in one action.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. A `member` calling `toggleFeatureFlagAction` is denied regardless of which flag they
   target.
2. `flag.toggled`'s payload identifies the flag key and the resulting override state
   (enabled, disabled, or cleared).
3. `toggleFlag` on a non-overridable flag fails before emitting the event (`REQ-190`), since
   no actual change occurred.

### REQ-193 — A disabled feature fails with FeatureDisabledError

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** ADR-014, REQ-138
- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/errors.ts` — `toAppError`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/errors.test.ts`

Attempting a gated action while its flag is off throws `FeatureDisabledError`, mapped by
`toAppError` to a distinct, specific `AppErrorShape` — not folded into `forbidden` or
`validation_failed` — so a client can distinguish "you don't have permission" from "this
isn't available on your plan or hasn't been rolled out to you yet" and render the
appropriate upsell or explanation.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. Every gated Server Action checks `isEnabled` and throws `FeatureDisabledError` rather
   than silently no-opping when the flag is off.
2. `FeatureDisabledError`'s mapped error code is distinct from `forbidden` and
   `plan_limit_exceeded`.
3. `tests/lib/errors.test.ts` covers `FeatureDisabledError`'s mapping alongside every other
   domain error class.

### REQ-194 — The client receives a flag snapshot, not the registry

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-186, DES-230
- **Implemented by:** `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` — `snapshotFlags`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`

`snapshotFlags()` produces a `FeatureFlagSnapshot` — a plain map of flag key to resolved
boolean for the current actor and org — that server components pass down to client
components, rather than shipping `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS` itself to the browser. This
keeps rollout percentages and plan thresholds server-side implementation detail, not
something inspectable from client-side JavaScript.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. No client bundle includes `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS` or the percentage-rollout hash
   input.
2. `FeatureFlagSnapshot` is computed once per request server-side and passed down, not
   recomputed independently by client components calling `isEnabled` themselves with a
   client-only context.
3. The snapshot reflects the same overrides and strategy evaluation the server would apply
   to a Server Action call in the same request.

### REQ-195 — Flag keys are a closed union

- **Priority:** must
- **Status:** implemented
- **Related:** REQ-185, DES-200
- **Implemented by:** `src/types/feature-flag.ts`, `src/schemas/feature-flag.ts`
- **Verified by:** `tests/lib/feature-flags.test.ts`

`FeatureFlagKey` in `src/types/feature-flag.ts` is a closed string-literal union matching
exactly the ten keys in `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS`; `src/schemas/feature-flag.ts` validates
any client-supplied flag key (for `toggleFeatureFlagAction`'s input) against this same union
at runtime, so a request naming an unknown flag key fails validation before it ever reaches
`toggleFlag`.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. `FeatureFlagKey`'s type and `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS`'s keys are kept in lockstep; a
   registry entry without a corresponding type member is a type error.
2. `toggleFeatureFlagSchema` rejects any flag key not in the closed union at the schema
   layer, before authorization or business logic runs.
3. Adding an eleventh flag requires updating both the type and the registry in the same
   change, never one without the other.

1	---
2	title: Settings — billing, flags and webhooks
3	id: UI-SETTINGS-BILLING
4	status: approved
5	owners: [r.saito, k.ferreira]

9	
10	# Settings — billing, flags and webhooks
11	
12	Four routes share this file: the billing page, invoice history, feature flag overrides, and
13	webhook endpoint management. Grouped together because all four are "plan-adjacent"
14	configuration screens — each one either changes what the org pays for or is itself gated by
15	what the org's plan already includes.
16	
17	## SCR-020 — Billing
18	
19	- **Route:** `/{orgSlug}/settings/billing`
20	- **Files:** `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/billing/page.tsx`
21	- **Server or client:** Server Component shell, plan-selection cards are interactive
22	- **Permission required:** `org:manage_billing` (owner only, per the `ROLE_MATRIX` table in
23	  `brief-common.md`) — 404 otherwise
24	- **Feature flag:** none
25	- **Data loaded:** `getBillingSummary(actor, org.id)` (`src/server/services/billing-service.ts`)
26	- **Components:** `BillingPlanCard` (`src/components/domain/billing/billing-plan-card.tsx`),
27	  `UsagePanel`
28	- **Actions invoked:** `changePlanAction` (`src/actions/billing/change-plan.ts`)
29	- **Satisfies:** REQ-130, REQ-131, REQ-140, REQ-141, REQ-142
30	- **Design:** DES-135, DES-136
31	
32	### Layout
33	
34	A header showing seats-on-plan and subscription status, a link to the invoice history route, a
35	"Usage" section rendering the full `UsagePanel` (identical component to the one on the org
36	overview, reused verbatim — see `screen-org-home.md`), and a "Plans" section: a two-column grid
37	of `BillingPlanCard`s, one per entry in `PLAN_IDS` (`src/types/billing.ts`), each rendered from
38	`getPlanLimits(plan)` so the numbers shown for every tier — free, starter, growth, enterprise —
39	come from the exact same `PlanLimits` table the quota guards elsewhere in the app enforce
40	against, never a separately maintained marketing copy of those numbers. A footer note under the
41	plan grid states the downgrade rule plainly: "Downgrading is refused while usage still exceeds
42	the target plan — free up seats or projects first."
43	
44	### Downgrades are checked against the target plan's limits before the switch
45	
46	`DES-136` is the design fact this screen's downgrade behavior visualizes: before a plan change
47	takes effect, every summary resource (seats, projects, issues, storage, API requests, webhooks)
48	is checked against the *target* plan's limits, not the current one — an org sitting at 40 seats
49	cannot downgrade to starter (10 seats) no matter how the request is framed, and the check runs
50	for the whole resource set at once rather than seat-by-seat. This page has no client-side
51	pre-check of its own; `selectPlan()` is a thin `"use server"` wrapper around `changePlanAction`,
52	so a downgrade attempt that would violate a limit surfaces only as the generic action error
53	`BillingPlanCard`'s `onSelect` handler receives — there is no separate warning rendered before
54	the click, which means an org close to a downgrade boundary discovers the refusal only by
55	attempting it. `REQ-141` is the requirement this enforces, and `REQ-140` is the companion
56	requirement covering the success path: a plan change, once accepted, emits `billing.plan_changed`.
57	
58	### SCR-021 — Invoices
59	
60	- **Route:** `/{orgSlug}/settings/billing/invoices`
61	- **Files:** `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/billing/invoices/page.tsx`
62	- **Server or client:** Server Component
63	- **Permission required:** `org:manage_billing`, the identical gate the billing page uses — the
64	  page's own doc comment notes this is deliberate, since invoices carry amounts and are not
65	  something a member should be able to browse even read-only
66	- **Feature flag:** none
67	- **Data loaded:** `listInvoices(actor, org.id)`
68	- **Components:** `InvoiceTable` (`src/components/domain/billing/invoice-table.tsx`),
69	  `EmptyState`
70	- **Actions invoked:** none — purely a read screen
71	- **Satisfies:** REQ-143
72	- **Design:** none directly at the design-doc layer beyond the billing service's general
73	  invoice generation coverage
74	
75	A single flat table, one row per billing period, newest first. `REQ-143` (invoices generated per
76	billing period) is the requirement this table visualizes; a free-plan org sees an `EmptyState`
77	("No invoices yet — Organizations on the free plan are never invoiced") since free orgs never
78	accrue a billed period in the first place.
79	
80	## SCR-022 — Feature flags
81	
82	- **Route:** `/{orgSlug}/settings/flags`
83	- **Files:** `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/flags/page.tsx`, list in
84	  `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/flags/flag-toggle-list.tsx`
85	- **Server or client:** Server Component shell, interactive toggle list
86	- **Permission required:** `org:manage_flags` (member and above) — 404 otherwise
87	- **Feature flag:** n/a — this page *is* the flag-management surface, not something a flag
88	  gates
89	- **Data loaded:** no service call beyond tenant context; the ten rows are built in-memory from
90	  `Object.values(FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS)` (`src/config/feature-flags.ts`) combined with
91	  `isEnabled()` evaluated once per flag and `org.settings.enabledFlagOverrides` (a `Set`) for
92	  the override state
93	- **Components:** `FlagToggleList`
94	- **Actions invoked:** `toggleFeatureFlagAction` (`src/actions/flags/toggle-flag.ts`)
95	- **Satisfies:** REQ-185, REQ-188, REQ-190, REQ-191, REQ-192
96	- **Design:** DES-175, DES-176, DES-177
97	
98	### Three separate facts per row, deliberately not conflated
99	
100	This page's own doc comment names the exact design tension it resolves: each row shows three
101	things that are easy to collapse into one but are not the same fact — what the flag definition's
102	*rollout strategy* says (rendered via a local `describeStrategy()` helper mapping `on`/`off`/
103	`plan`/`role`/`percentage` to plain-English labels: "Always on," "Off by default," "Included from
104	a certain plan," "Limited by role," "Percentage rollout"), whether the *organization has an
105	override* set (`overridden`, from the `enabledFlagOverrides` set), and what `isEnabled()`
106	*actually evaluates to right now* (`enabled`, which folds the override, the strategy, and the
107	org's current plan/role context together). A row can show "Included from a certain plan" as its
108	strategy while still showing `enabled: false` if the org's current plan does not meet the
109	threshold, and a row can show `enabled: true` purely because of an override even though its
110	strategy alone would evaluate false — the three columns exist precisely so an admin can tell
111	those cases apart rather than only seeing the final boolean.
112	
113	Only `overridable` flags (per `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS[key].overridable`) accept a toggle in
114	`FlagToggleList` — `command_palette` and `webhooks` are both `NOT overridable` per
115	`brief-common.md`'s registry, so their rows render without a working switch regardless of the
116	viewing admin's role. `DES-177` is the authorization fact behind the toggle itself: `toggleFlag`
117	checks overridability against the *registry*, not against role rank — an admin cannot force an
118	override onto a non-overridable flag no matter how the request is crafted, because the guard is a
119	property of the flag definition, not a permission check that a higher role could satisfy. `REQ-192`
120	requires that a successful toggle emits `flag.toggled`, and `DES-177` adds that the emitted event
121	carries a *re-evaluation* of the result rather than trusting whatever the client requested —
122	so a listener reacting to `flag.toggled` always sees the actual post-toggle state, not the
123	client's intent.
124	
125	## SCR-023 — Webhooks
126	
127	- **Route:** `/{orgSlug}/settings/webhooks`
128	- **Files:** `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/webhooks/page.tsx`, manager in
129	  `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/webhooks/webhook-manager.tsx`
130	- **Server or client:** Server Component shell, interactive manager
131	- **Permission required:** `webhook:manage` (admin and above) — 404 when absent
132	- **Feature flag:** `webhooks` (plan >= growth, **not** overridable)
133	- **Data loaded:** `getPlanLimits(org.plan)` for the endpoint ceiling, `listWebhooks(actor,
134	  org.id)` (`src/server/services/webhook-service.ts`) — but only once the flag check passes
135	- **Components:** `WebhookManager`, `EmptyState`
136	- **Actions invoked:** `createWebhookAction` (`src/actions/webhooks/create-webhook.ts`),
137	  `deleteWebhookAction` (`src/actions/webhooks/delete-webhook.ts`)
138	- **Satisfies:** REQ-150, REQ-151, REQ-152, REQ-153, REQ-159, REQ-161
139	- **Design:** DES-159, DES-160, DES-161, DES-257, DES-258
140	
141	### Three gates, and only the first one is a wall
142	
143	This page's own doc comment lays out its gating order deliberately: permission (`webhook:manage`
144	— may you manage webhooks at all), flag (`webhooks` — is the surface available on this plan),
145	and quota (`endpoints.length >= limits.webhooks` — how many more you may add). Only the first is
146	a hard `notFound()`; the other two render as *explanations* rather than blocking navigation. A
147	disabled `webhooks` flag produces an `EmptyState` ("Webhooks are not part of this plan — Upgrade
148	in Settings → Billing…") and skips `listWebhooks` entirely, identical in shape to the
149	`activity_feed` gate documented in `screen-activity.md`. A reached quota does not block the page
150	from rendering at all — `WebhookManager` receives `atLimit={endpoints.length >= limits.webhooks}`
151	as a prop and is expected to disable its own "add endpoint" affordance internally, so existing
152	endpoints remain fully manageable (editable, deletable, testable) even once the org can create no
153	more.
154	
155	`DES-257` is the design fact that explains why this page checks the flag and the quota as two
156	genuinely independent conditions rather than deriving one from the other: an *override* can force
157	the flag on without touching the numeric ceiling, since `webhooks` (the flag) governs whether the
158	feature surface exists at all while `limits.webhooks` (the quota, from `PlanLimits`) governs how
159	many endpoints the plan permits — a growth-plan org with the flag on by its normal plan gate and
160	a starter-plan org with the flag force-enabled by an override face the same quota math once
161	they're both past the flag check, because the quota is read straight from `getPlanLimits(org.plan)`
162	regardless of how the flag itself was satisfied.
163	
164	### Secret minted once, never regenerated
165	
166	`DES-159` documents a fact this screen's create flow depends on but does not surface visually
167	beyond a one-time reveal (handled inside `WebhookManager`, not this page): an endpoint's signing
168	secret is minted exactly once at creation and never regenerated — there is no "rotate secret"
169	action anywhere in the manifest for this screen, `create-webhook.ts` and `delete-webhook.ts` are
170	the only two mutations wired here. `DES-258` explains why `deleteWebhookAction` is deliberately
171	**not** flag-gated the way creation is: a downgraded organization that has lost the `webhooks`
172	flag must still be able to clean up its existing endpoints, so delete works even when the create
173	button and the rest of the page's normal content have already fallen back to the "not part of
174	this plan" `EmptyState` — practically, this means an org that downgrades below growth still needs
175	some path back into this page to delete stale endpoints, which the flag-off `EmptyState` as
176	currently written does not obviously provide, since the whole manager (delete button included)
177	is skipped when the flag check fails before `listWebhooks` ever runs. This is a known rough edge
178	worth flagging rather than glossing over: the design intent (`DES-258`) and the page's literal
179	control flow (flag-off short-circuits to `EmptyState` before the manager renders at all) do not
180	fully agree, and reconciling them is open in the same ops backlog referenced in
181	`screen-search.md`'s notes on copy/behavior drift.
182	
183	### States
184	
185	| state | screen | trigger | what the user sees |
186	|---|---|---|---|
187	| empty | invoices | zero invoices, typically a free-plan org | `EmptyState`: "No invoices yet" |
188	| loading | all four | client navigation | `[orgSlug]/loading.tsx` — none of these four define a dedicated `loading.tsx` |
189	| error | all four | thrown error resolving tenant context or a service call | `[orgSlug]/error.tsx` |
190	| permission denied | all four | `org:manage_billing` / `org:manage_flags` / `webhook:manage` fails | `notFound()` |
191	| flag off | webhooks | `webhooks` flag false for the org's plan | `EmptyState`: "Webhooks are not part of this plan," no endpoint list fetched |
192	| plan limit reached | billing | downgrade target plan's limits exceeded by current usage | Generic action error on `selectPlan()`, no pre-emptive client-side warning |
193	| plan limit reached | webhooks | `endpoints.length >= limits.webhooks` | `WebhookManager` renders existing endpoints normally; its create control is disabled via `atLimit` |
194

### SCR-021 — Invoices

- **Route:** `/{orgSlug}/settings/billing/invoices`
- **Files:** `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/billing/invoices/page.tsx`
- **Server or client:** Server Component
- **Permission required:** `org:manage_billing`, the identical gate the billing page uses — the
  page's own doc comment notes this is deliberate, since invoices carry amounts and are not
  something a member should be able to browse even read-only
- **Feature flag:** none
- **Data loaded:** `listInvoices(actor, org.id)`
- **Components:** `InvoiceTable` (`src/components/domain/billing/invoice-table.tsx`),
  `EmptyState`
- **Actions invoked:** none — purely a read screen
- **Satisfies:** REQ-143
- **Design:** none directly at the design-doc layer beyond the billing service's general
  invoice generation coverage

A single flat table, one row per billing period, newest first. `REQ-143` (invoices generated per
billing period) is the requirement this table visualizes; a free-plan org sees an `EmptyState`
("No invoices yet — Organizations on the free plan are never invoiced") since free orgs never
accrue a billed period in the first place.

## SCR-022 — Feature flags

- **Route:** `/{orgSlug}/settings/flags`
- **Files:** `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/flags/page.tsx`, list in
  `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/flags/flag-toggle-list.tsx`
- **Server or client:** Server Component shell, interactive toggle list
- **Permission required:** `org:manage_flags` (member and above) — 404 otherwise
- **Feature flag:** n/a — this page *is* the flag-management surface, not something a flag
  gates
- **Data loaded:** no service call beyond tenant context; the ten rows are built in-memory from
  `Object.values(FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS)` (`src/config/feature-flags.ts`) combined with
  `isEnabled()` evaluated once per flag and `org.settings.enabledFlagOverrides` (a `Set`) for
  the override state
- **Components:** `FlagToggleList`
- **Actions invoked:** `toggleFeatureFlagAction` (`src/actions/flags/toggle-flag.ts`)
- **Satisfies:** REQ-185, REQ-188, REQ-190, REQ-191, REQ-192
- **Design:** DES-175, DES-176, DES-177

### Three separate facts per row, deliberately not conflated

This page's own doc comment names the exact design tension it resolves: each row shows three
things that are easy to collapse into one but are not the same fact — what the flag definition's
*rollout strategy* says (rendered via a local `describeStrategy()` helper mapping `on`/`off`/
`plan`/`role`/`percentage` to plain-English labels: "Always on," "Off by default," "Included from
a certain plan," "Limited by role," "Percentage rollout"), whether the *organization has an
override* set (`overridden`, from the `enabledFlagOverrides` set), and what `isEnabled()`
*actually evaluates to right now* (`enabled`, which folds the override, the strategy, and the
org's current plan/role context together). A row can show "Included from a certain plan" as its
strategy while still showing `enabled: false` if the org's current plan does not meet the
threshold, and a row can show `enabled: true` purely because of an override even though its
strategy alone would evaluate false — the three columns exist precisely so an admin can tell
those cases apart rather than only seeing the final boolean.

Only `overridable` flags (per `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS[key].overridable`) accept a toggle in
`FlagToggleList` — `command_palette` and `webhooks` are both `NOT overridable` per
`brief-common.md`'s registry, so their rows render without a working switch regardless of the
viewing admin's role. `DES-177` is the authorization fact behind the toggle itself: `toggleFlag`
checks overridability against the *registry*, not against role rank — an admin cannot force an
override onto a non-overridable flag no matter how the request is crafted, because the guard is a
property of the flag definition, not a permission check that a higher role could satisfy. `REQ-192`
requires that a successful toggle emits `flag.toggled`, and `DES-177` adds that the emitted event
carries a *re-evaluation* of the result rather than trusting whatever the client requested —
so a listener reacting to `flag.toggled` always sees the actual post-toggle state, not the
client's intent.

## SCR-023 — Webhooks

- **Route:** `/{orgSlug}/settings/webhooks`
- **Files:** `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/webhooks/page.tsx`, manager in
  `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/webhooks/webhook-manager.tsx`
- **Server or client:** Server Component shell, interactive manager
- **Permission required:** `webhook:manage` (admin and above) — 404 when absent
- **Feature flag:** `webhooks` (plan >= growth, **not** overridable)
- **Data loaded:** `getPlanLimits(org.plan)` for the endpoint ceiling, `listWebhooks(actor,
  org.id)` (`src/server/services/webhook-service.ts`) — but only once the flag check passes
- **Components:** `WebhookManager`, `EmptyState`
- **Actions invoked:** `createWebhookAction` (`src/actions/webhooks/create-webhook.ts`),
  `deleteWebhookAction` (`src/actions/webhooks/delete-webhook.ts`)
- **Satisfies:** REQ-150, REQ-151, REQ-152, REQ-153, REQ-159, REQ-161
- **Design:** DES-159, DES-160, DES-161, DES-257, DES-258

### Three gates, and only the first one is a wall

This page's own doc comment lays out its gating order deliberately: permission (`webhook:manage`
— may you manage webhooks at all), flag (`webhooks` — is the surface available on this plan),
and quota (`endpoints.length >= limits.webhooks` — how many more you may add). Only the first is
a hard `notFound()`; the other two render as *explanations* rather than blocking navigation. A
disabled `webhooks` flag produces an `EmptyState` ("Webhooks are not part of this plan — Upgrade
in Settings → Billing…") and skips `listWebhooks` entirely, identical in shape to the
`activity_feed` gate documented in `screen-activity.md`. A reached quota does not block the page
from rendering at all — `WebhookManager` receives `atLimit={endpoints.length >= limits.webhooks}`
as a prop and is expected to disable its own "add endpoint" affordance internally, so existing
endpoints remain fully manageable (editable, deletable, testable) even once the org can create no
more.

`DES-257` is the design fact that explains why this page checks the flag and the quota as two
genuinely independent conditions rather than deriving one from the other: an *override* can force
the flag on without touching the numeric ceiling, since `webhooks` (the flag) governs whether the
feature surface exists at all while `limits.webhooks` (the quota, from `PlanLimits`) governs how
many endpoints the plan permits — a growth-plan org with the flag on by its normal plan gate and
a starter-plan org with the flag force-enabled by an override face the same quota math once
they're both past the flag check, because the quota is read straight from `getPlanLimits(org.plan)`
regardless of how the flag itself was satisfied.

### Secret minted once, never regenerated

`DES-159` documents a fact this screen's create flow depends on but does not surface visually
beyond a one-time reveal (handled inside `WebhookManager`, not this page): an endpoint's signing
secret is minted exactly once at creation and never regenerated — there is no "rotate secret"
action anywhere in the manifest for this screen, `create-webhook.ts` and `delete-webhook.ts` are
the only two mutations wired here. `DES-258` explains why `deleteWebhookAction` is deliberately
**not** flag-gated the way creation is: a downgraded organization that has lost the `webhooks`
flag must still be able to clean up its existing endpoints, so delete works even when the create
button and the rest of the page's normal content have already fallen back to the "not part of
this plan" `EmptyState` — practically, this means an org that downgrades below growth still needs
some path back into this page to delete stale endpoints, which the flag-off `EmptyState` as
currently written does not obviously provide, since the whole manager (delete button included)
is skipped when the flag check fails before `listWebhooks` ever runs. This is a known rough edge
worth flagging rather than glossing over: the design intent (`DES-258`) and the page's literal
control flow (flag-off short-circuits to `EmptyState` before the manager renders at all) do not
fully agree, and reconciling them is open in the same ops backlog referenced in
`screen-search.md`'s notes on copy/behavior drift.

### States

| state | screen | trigger | what the user sees |
|---|---|---|---|
| empty | invoices | zero invoices, typically a free-plan org | `EmptyState`: "No invoices yet" |
| loading | all four | client navigation | `[orgSlug]/loading.tsx` — none of these four define a dedicated `loading.tsx` |
| error | all four | thrown error resolving tenant context or a service call | `[orgSlug]/error.tsx` |
| permission denied | all four | `org:manage_billing` / `org:manage_flags` / `webhook:manage` fails | `notFound()` |
| flag off | webhooks | `webhooks` flag false for the org's plan | `EmptyState`: "Webhooks are not part of this plan," no endpoint list fetched |
| plan limit reached | billing | downgrade target plan's limits exceeded by current usage | Generic action error on `selectPlan()`, no pre-emptive client-side warning |
| plan limit reached | webhooks | `endpoints.length >= limits.webhooks` | `WebhookManager` renders existing endpoints normally; its create control is disabled via `atLimit` |

1	---
2	title: Issue detail
3	id: UI-ISSUE-DETAIL
4	status: approved
5	owners: [m.lindqvist]
6	last_updated: 2026-08-12
7	related: [REQ-090, REQ-092, REQ-097, DES-106, DES-115, DES-117, ADR-015]
8	---
9	
10	# Issue detail
11	
12	## SCR-010 — Issue detail
13	
14	- **Route:** `/{orgSlug}/projects/{projectSlug}/issues/{issueNumber}`
15	- **Files:** `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/projects/[projectSlug]/issues/[issueNumber]/page.tsx`,
16	  with dedicated `error.tsx`, `loading.tsx` and `not-found.tsx` siblings in the same segment
17	- **Server or client:** Server Component shell; `CommentComposer`, `CommentThread` and
18	  `IssueDetail` render interactive sub-trees but the page itself does no client work
19	- **Permission required:** `issue:read`, checked against the *resolved row* (`found.authorId`,
20	  `found.assigneeId`) rather than a pending placeholder — this is one of the few screens where
21	  the permission resource is built from real data instead of `PENDING_ISSUE_ID`
22	- **Feature flag:** none
23	- **Data loaded:** `findIssueByNumber(org.id, project.id, number)`
24	  (`src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts`) to resolve the human-facing number to a row;
25	  then, in parallel, `getIssue(actor, org.id, found.id)`, `getThread(actor, org.id, found.id)`
26	  (`src/server/services/comment-service.ts`), `listMembers(actor, { orgId, limit: 100 })`,
27	  `listActivityForSubject(org.id, "issue", found.id)`
28	  (`src/server/repositories/activity-repository.ts`), `findUserById(found.authorId)`
29	  (`src/server/repositories/user-repository.ts`), and conditionally `findUserById` for the
30	  assignee
31	- **Components:** `IssueDetail` (`src/components/domain/issue/issue-detail.tsx`),
32	  `CommentThread` (`src/components/domain/comment/comment-thread.tsx`), `CommentComposer`
33	  (`src/components/domain/comment/comment-composer.tsx`), `IssueActivityPanel`
34	  (`src/components/domain/issue/issue-activity-panel.tsx`)
35	- **Actions invoked:** `createCommentAction` (`src/actions/comments/create-comment.ts`),
36	  `deleteCommentAction` (`src/actions/comments/delete-comment.ts`) — wired through a local
37	  server function bound with `"use server"` rather than passed as a plain action reference,
38	  because it needs to close over `org.id`
39	- **Satisfies:** REQ-090, REQ-092, REQ-097, REQ-098
40	- **Design:** DES-106, DES-115, DES-117, DES-119
41	
42	### Layout
43	
44	A two-column grid on large screens (`grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_18rem]`) that collapses to one
45	column below the `lg` breakpoint. The left column holds `IssueDetail` (title, description,
46	status, priority, due date, assignee and label metadata rail — all read-only display here; edits
47	happen through the pickers embedded inside `IssueDetail` itself, which is why this page does not
48	separately import `IssueStatusSelect` or `IssueAssigneePicker`), followed by a "Comments"
49	section: `CommentThread` rendering every node with reply-depth indentation, and `CommentComposer`
50	below it for posting a new top-level comment. The right column is `IssueActivityPanel`, a
51	per-issue slice of the audit trail scoped by `listActivityForSubject`.
52	
53	### Resolving the number is itself the tenant boundary
54	
55	The URL segment `[issueNumber]` is the human-facing sequence number (`REQ-061`: allocated per
56	project, never reused), not the issue's branded id. `findIssueByNumber(org.id, project.id,
57	number)` is deliberately called with *both* `org.id` and `project.id` — the page's own doc
58	comment states plainly that the number is only unique within a project, so a lookup scoped to
59	the number alone would leak issues across every project that happens to share the same numeric
60	sequence. This lookup is not merely a convenience query; it is where tenant scoping happens for
61	this screen, before any permission check runs. A malformed or non-positive `issueNumber` (parsed
62	with `Number.parseInt`) triggers `notFound()` immediately, and a `found === null` result — the
63	number does not exist in this project — triggers the identical `notFound()`, so a caller cannot
64	distinguish "not a number" from "no such issue" from the response.
65	
66	### `getIssue` composes without separately authorizing the pieces
67	
68	`DES-106` is the design fact this page's data-loading shape exists to satisfy: `getIssue`
69	combines the issue row, its author, and its assignee into one read model, and it does *not*
70	re-authorize each composed piece independently — the single `issue:read` check performed against
71	`found` before any of the parallel fetches covers the whole assembled view. This is why the page
72	can safely fire `getIssue`, `getThread`, `listMembers`, `listActivityForSubject` and two
73	`findUserById` calls all inside one `Promise.all` without threading a fresh permission check
74	through each one: the gate already ran, and everything fetched afterward belongs to the same
75	authorized view. `getThread` is the one exception worth naming, because it is *not* fully
76	subsumed by the outer check — `DES-119` documents that `getThread` re-checks `comment:read`
77	itself even though the caller already proved they can read the parent issue, since comment
78	visibility and issue visibility are governed by separate `ROLE_MATRIX` entries that happen to
79	share a minimum role today but are not guaranteed to stay aligned.
80	
81	### Comment composition, mentions, and the fifteen-minute self-edit window
82	
83	`CommentComposer` binds to `createCommentSchema` and passes the member list so `@mention`
84	autocomplete (via `MentionTextarea`, `src/components/domain/comment/mention-textarea.tsx`) can
85	resolve names to `UserId`s client-side — but `DES-116` is explicit that the *server's* mention
86	parse is what actually wins on disagreement with whatever the client reported; the client-side
87	resolution exists for autocomplete UX, not as a trusted mention list. `DES-115` documents that
88	comment creation is rate-limited (`comment:create`, 60 capacity / 20 refill-per-minute,
89	`src/lib/rate-limit.ts`) *before* mentions are resolved, so a burst of comment submissions never
90	reaches the member-scan step at all — this page has no visible rate-limit affordance, so a
91	throttled submission surfaces only as the generic `ActionResult` error rendered by
92	`useFormAction`'s `error` state inside `CommentComposer`.
93	
94	`CommentThread` hides the delete control for anyone but the comment's own author, tied to
95	`REQ-097` (authors may edit their own comments) and its companion delete rule; `DES-117` narrows
96	this further for *editing* specifically — the self-edit window is author-only and closes fifteen
97	minutes after posting, a constraint this page's UI does not visibly count down but which the
98	underlying `update-comment` action enforces server-side, so an edit attempted after the window
99	fails with the generic action error rather than a client-side disabled state (there is no client
100	clock check here, deliberately — see `DES-239` in the action layer for why the check is
101	authoritative server-side).
102	
103	### `IssueDetail`'s metadata rail
104	
105	`IssueDetailProps` is `{ issue: IssueWithRelations, actor, author, assignee }`. The component
106	renders the issue title and description as the primary column and a metadata rail alongside it
107	carrying status (`IssueStatusSelect`, driven by the closed `ISSUE_STATUSES` union), priority
108	(`IssuePrioritySelect`, driven by `ISSUE_PRIORITIES`), the due date (`IssueDueDateField`, which
109	visually flags a past-due value), the assignee (`IssueAssigneePicker`, restricted to active
110	members of the org so a removed member can never be re-assigned an issue through this control),
111	and the label set (`IssueLabelPicker`, multi-select against the org's shared label list — see
112	`screen-settings-org-and-members.md`'s labels screen for where those labels are managed). Every
113	one of these pickers is permission-gated independently inside `IssueDetail` rather than the page
114	disabling the whole component when `issue:update` fails — a viewer who can only read the issue
115	sees every field rendered read-only, while a member who owns the issue by authorship or
116	assignment sees the fields they are specifically permitted to change become interactive, which is
117	the ownership-escalation story from `screen-project-board.md` playing out again here at the
118	per-field level rather than the per-card level.
119	
120	`IssueId`, `ProjectId`, `OrgId` and the rest of the branded id types this page threads through
121	its data-loading calls are `ADR-015`'s branded-string-id pattern in practice: `findIssueByNumber`
122	returns a row whose `.id` is already typed as `IssueId`, not a bare `string`, so the subsequent
123	`getIssue(actor, org.id, found.id)` call cannot accidentally be passed a `ProjectId` or a raw
124	unvalidated string that happens to look like an id — a mistake the type checker catches at
125	compile time rather than a bug discovered at runtime against the wrong tenant's row.
126	
127	### Editing and deleting a comment from this page
128	
129	`CommentItem` (`src/components/domain/comment/comment-item.tsx`, rendered inside
130	`CommentThread` for each node) exposes an `onEdit?` callback distinct from the page-level
131	`onDelete` this page wires up explicitly — editing is handled entirely inside the comment
132	component's own local state and its own binding to the update action, while deletion is the one
133	mutation this page threads through as a named server function (`deleteComment`, closing over
134	`org.id`) because `CommentThread`'s `onDelete` prop is required, not optional, in its type
135	signature. This asymmetry — delete wired explicitly by the page, edit handled internally by the
136	component — reflects that deletion needs no form state (it is a single confirm-and-fire action)
137	while editing needs the composer's full validation and error-rendering machinery, which
138	`CommentItem` already owns internally rather than duplicating at the page level.
139	
140	`CommentThread`'s `depth` prop on each node is what drives the reply-chain indentation; Taskflow's
141	comment model supports threaded replies (a comment can reply to another comment on the same
142	issue), and `DES-186` — cited fully in the design catalogue rather than reproduced here — notes
143	that archived (soft-deleted) replies are deliberately kept in the thread rather than removed, so
144	that a live reply never loses the anchor comment it was responding to. This page's rendering of
145	`thread` therefore may include comment nodes whose body has been replaced with deleted-comment
146	placeholder copy inside `CommentItem`, sitting beside their still-live replies, rather than the
147	thread silently closing the gap.
148	
149	### `IssueActivityPanel` versus the full activity feed
150	
151	The right-column `IssueActivityPanel` (`{ events: readonly ActivityEvent[], actors }`) is
152	populated from `listActivityForSubject(org.id, "issue", found.id)` — a query scoped to exactly
153	this one issue's audit trail, not the organization-wide feed `screen-activity.md` documents.
154	The two surfaces share the same underlying `ActivityEvent` shape and the same nine event types
155	`DES-173` names, but `IssueActivityPanel` renders no day-grouping, no export button, and no
156	permission gate of its own beyond what already gated the whole page — since a caller who can
157	read this issue at all is trusted to see its own activity history, unlike the organization-wide
158	feed, which requires the separate `activity:read` permission and the `activity_feed` flag on top
159	of ordinary issue-read access.
160	
161	### States
162	
163	| state | trigger | what the user sees |
164	|---|---|---|
165	| empty | issue has zero comments | `CommentThread` renders nothing above the composer — no explicit "no comments yet" `EmptyState` is used on this screen, since the composer itself is always visible and self-explanatory. |
166	| loading | client navigation to an issue's detail route | `issues/[issueNumber]/loading.tsx`, a skeleton scoped to just this segment. |
167	| error | any thrown error after the issue is resolved (e.g. a transient failure in `listActivityForSubject`) | `issues/[issueNumber]/error.tsx`, a dedicated boundary for this segment (distinct from the tenant-level `[orgSlug]/error.tsx`, giving issue-specific errors their own reset scope). |
168	| permission denied | `issue:read` fails against the resolved row | `notFound()` — identical response to an issue number that does not exist at all. |
169	| flag off | none apply to this screen | — |
170	| plan limit reached | not applicable directly, though a comment attempt against an org that has hit `apiRequestsPerHour` could surface a `rate_limited` action error | Generic `ActionResult` error rendered inline by `CommentComposer`'s `useFormAction` binding, not a dedicated banner. |

---
title: Issue detail
id: UI-ISSUE-DETAIL
status: approved
owners: [m.lindqvist]
last_updated: 2026-08-12
related: [REQ-090, REQ-092, REQ-097, DES-106, DES-115, DES-117, ADR-015]
---

# Issue detail

## SCR-010 — Issue detail

- **Route:** `/{orgSlug}/projects/{projectSlug}/issues/{issueNumber}`
- **Files:** `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/projects/[projectSlug]/issues/[issueNumber]/page.tsx`,
  with dedicated `error.tsx`, `loading.tsx` and `not-found.tsx` siblings in the same segment
- **Server or client:** Server Component shell; `CommentComposer`, `CommentThread` and
  `IssueDetail` render interactive sub-trees but the page itself does no client work
- **Permission required:** `issue:read`, checked against the *resolved row* (`found.authorId`,
  `found.assigneeId`) rather than a pending placeholder — this is one of the few screens where
  the permission resource is built from real data instead of `PENDING_ISSUE_ID`
- **Feature flag:** none
- **Data loaded:** `findIssueByNumber(org.id, project.id, number)`
  (`src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts`) to resolve the human-facing number to a row;
  then, in parallel, `getIssue(actor, org.id, found.id)`, `getThread(actor, org.id, found.id)`
  (`src/server/services/comment-service.ts`), `listMembers(actor, { orgId, limit: 100 })`,
  `listActivityForSubject(org.id, "issue", found.id)`
  (`src/server/repositories/activity-repository.ts`), `findUserById(found.authorId)`
  (`src/server/repositories/user-repository.ts`), and conditionally `findUserById` for the
  assignee
- **Components:** `IssueDetail` (`src/components/domain/issue/issue-detail.tsx`),
  `CommentThread` (`src/components/domain/comment/comment-thread.tsx`), `CommentComposer`
  (`src/components/domain/comment/comment-composer.tsx`), `IssueActivityPanel`
  (`src/components/domain/issue/issue-activity-panel.tsx`)
- **Actions invoked:** `createCommentAction` (`src/actions/comments/create-comment.ts`),
  `deleteCommentAction` (`src/actions/comments/delete-comment.ts`) — wired through a local
  server function bound with `"use server"` rather than passed as a plain action reference,
  because it needs to close over `org.id`
- **Satisfies:** REQ-090, REQ-092, REQ-097, REQ-098
- **Design:** DES-106, DES-115, DES-117, DES-119

### Layout

A two-column grid on large screens (`grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_18rem]`) that collapses to one
column below the `lg` breakpoint. The left column holds `IssueDetail` (title, description,
status, priority, due date, assignee and label metadata rail — all read-only display here; edits
happen through the pickers embedded inside `IssueDetail` itself, which is why this page does not
separately import `IssueStatusSelect` or `IssueAssigneePicker`), followed by a "Comments"
section: `CommentThread` rendering every node with reply-depth indentation, and `CommentComposer`
below it for posting a new top-level comment. The right column is `IssueActivityPanel`, a
per-issue slice of the audit trail scoped by `listActivityForSubject`.

### Resolving the number is itself the tenant boundary

The URL segment `[issueNumber]` is the human-facing sequence number (`REQ-061`: allocated per
project, never reused), not the issue's branded id. `findIssueByNumber(org.id, project.id,
number)` is deliberately called with *both* `org.id` and `project.id` — the page's own doc
comment states plainly that the number is only unique within a project, so a lookup scoped to
the number alone would leak issues across every project that happens to share the same numeric
sequence. This lookup is not merely a convenience query; it is where tenant scoping happens for
this screen, before any permission check runs. A malformed or non-positive `issueNumber` (parsed
with `Number.parseInt`) triggers `notFound()` immediately, and a `found === null` result — the
number does not exist in this project — triggers the identical `notFound()`, so a caller cannot
distinguish "not a number" from "no such issue" from the response.

### `getIssue` composes without separately authorizing the pieces

`DES-106` is the design fact this page's data-loading shape exists to satisfy: `getIssue`
combines the issue row, its author, and its assignee into one read model, and it does *not*
re-authorize each composed piece independently — the single `issue:read` check performed against
`found` before any of the parallel fetches covers the whole assembled view. This is why the page
can safely fire `getIssue`, `getThread`, `listMembers`, `listActivityForSubject` and two
`findUserById` calls all inside one `Promise.all` without threading a fresh permission check
through each one: the gate already ran, and everything fetched afterward belongs to the same
authorized view. `getThread` is the one exception worth naming, because it is *not* fully
subsumed by the outer check — `DES-119` documents that `getThread` re-checks `comment:read`
itself even though the caller already proved they can read the parent issue, since comment
visibility and issue visibility are governed by separate `ROLE_MATRIX` entries that happen to
share a minimum role today but are not guaranteed to stay aligned.

### Comment composition, mentions, and the fifteen-minute self-edit window

`CommentComposer` binds to `createCommentSchema` and passes the member list so `@mention`
autocomplete (via `MentionTextarea`, `src/components/domain/comment/mention-textarea.tsx`) can
resolve names to `UserId`s client-side — but `DES-116` is explicit that the *server's* mention
parse is what actually wins on disagreement with whatever the client reported; the client-side
resolution exists for autocomplete UX, not as a trusted mention list. `DES-115` documents that
comment creation is rate-limited (`comment:create`, 60 capacity / 20 refill-per-minute,
`src/lib/rate-limit.ts`) *before* mentions are resolved, so a burst of comment submissions never
reaches the member-scan step at all — this page has no visible rate-limit affordance, so a
throttled submission surfaces only as the generic `ActionResult` error rendered by
`useFormAction`'s `error` state inside `CommentComposer`.

`CommentThread` hides the delete control for anyone but the comment's own author, tied to
`REQ-097` (authors may edit their own comments) and its companion delete rule; `DES-117` narrows
this further for *editing* specifically — the self-edit window is author-only and closes fifteen
minutes after posting, a constraint this page's UI does not visibly count down but which the
underlying `update-comment` action enforces server-side, so an edit attempted after the window
fails with the generic action error rather than a client-side disabled state (there is no client
clock check here, deliberately — see `DES-239` in the action layer for why the check is
authoritative server-side).

### `IssueDetail`'s metadata rail

`IssueDetailProps` is `{ issue: IssueWithRelations, actor, author, assignee }`. The component
renders the issue title and description as the primary column and a metadata rail alongside it
carrying status (`IssueStatusSelect`, driven by the closed `ISSUE_STATUSES` union), priority
(`IssuePrioritySelect`, driven by `ISSUE_PRIORITIES`), the due date (`IssueDueDateField`, which
visually flags a past-due value), the assignee (`IssueAssigneePicker`, restricted to active
members of the org so a removed member can never be re-assigned an issue through this control),
and the label set (`IssueLabelPicker`, multi-select against the org's shared label list — see
`screen-settings-org-and-members.md`'s labels screen for where those labels are managed). Every
one of these pickers is permission-gated independently inside `IssueDetail` rather than the page
disabling the whole component when `issue:update` fails — a viewer who can only read the issue
sees every field rendered read-only, while a member who owns the issue by authorship or
assignment sees the fields they are specifically permitted to change become interactive, which is
the ownership-escalation story from `screen-project-board.md` playing out again here at the
per-field level rather than the per-card level.

`IssueId`, `ProjectId`, `OrgId` and the rest of the branded id types this page threads through
its data-loading calls are `ADR-015`'s branded-string-id pattern in practice: `findIssueByNumber`
returns a row whose `.id` is already typed as `IssueId`, not a bare `string`, so the subsequent
`getIssue(actor, org.id, found.id)` call cannot accidentally be passed a `ProjectId` or a raw
unvalidated string that happens to look like an id — a mistake the type checker catches at
compile time rather than a bug discovered at runtime against the wrong tenant's row.

### Editing and deleting a comment from this page

`CommentItem` (`src/components/domain/comment/comment-item.tsx`, rendered inside
`CommentThread` for each node) exposes an `onEdit?` callback distinct from the page-level
`onDelete` this page wires up explicitly — editing is handled entirely inside the comment
component's own local state and its own binding to the update action, while deletion is the one
mutation this page threads through as a named server function (`deleteComment`, closing over
`org.id`) because `CommentThread`'s `onDelete` prop is required, not optional, in its type
signature. This asymmetry — delete wired explicitly by the page, edit handled internally by the
component — reflects that deletion needs no form state (it is a single confirm-and-fire action)
while editing needs the composer's full validation and error-rendering machinery, which
`CommentItem` already owns internally rather than duplicating at the page level.

`CommentThread`'s `depth` prop on each node is what drives the reply-chain indentation; Taskflow's
comment model supports threaded replies (a comment can reply to another comment on the same
issue), and `DES-186` — cited fully in the design catalogue rather than reproduced here — notes
that archived (soft-deleted) replies are deliberately kept in the thread rather than removed, so
that a live reply never loses the anchor comment it was responding to. This page's rendering of
`thread` therefore may include comment nodes whose body has been replaced with deleted-comment
placeholder copy inside `CommentItem`, sitting beside their still-live replies, rather than the
thread silently closing the gap.

### `IssueActivityPanel` versus the full activity feed

The right-column `IssueActivityPanel` (`{ events: readonly ActivityEvent[], actors }`) is
populated from `listActivityForSubject(org.id, "issue", found.id)` — a query scoped to exactly
this one issue's audit trail, not the organization-wide feed `screen-activity.md` documents.
The two surfaces share the same underlying `ActivityEvent` shape and the same nine event types
`DES-173` names, but `IssueActivityPanel` renders no day-grouping, no export button, and no
permission gate of its own beyond what already gated the whole page — since a caller who can
read this issue at all is trusted to see its own activity history, unlike the organization-wide
feed, which requires the separate `activity:read` permission and the `activity_feed` flag on top
of ordinary issue-read access.

### States

| state | trigger | what the user sees |
|---|---|---|
| empty | issue has zero comments | `CommentThread` renders nothing above the composer — no explicit "no comments yet" `EmptyState` is used on this screen, since the composer itself is always visible and self-explanatory. |
| loading | client navigation to an issue's detail route | `issues/[issueNumber]/loading.tsx`, a skeleton scoped to just this segment. |
| error | any thrown error after the issue is resolved (e.g. a transient failure in `listActivityForSubject`) | `issues/[issueNumber]/error.tsx`, a dedicated boundary for this segment (distinct from the tenant-level `[orgSlug]/error.tsx`, giving issue-specific errors their own reset scope). |
| permission denied | `issue:read` fails against the resolved row | `notFound()` — identical response to an issue number that does not exist at all. |
| flag off | none apply to this screen | — |
| plan limit reached | not applicable directly, though a comment attempt against an org that has hit `apiRequestsPerHour` could surface a `rate_limited` action error | Generic `ActionResult` error rendered inline by `CommentComposer`'s `useFormAction` binding, not a dedicated banner. |

lastPrompt: Consider the area of role-based permission gates: who is allowed to write a comment, who is allowed to archive a project, and who is allowed to open the feature-flag settings screen. Somewhere in that…
